AppConstantsResponse.title: AppConstantsResponse
AppConstantsResponse.description:
Shared domain constants that the frontend must stay in sync with.

The frontend fetches this once on app init so both layers
always agree on categories, interest mappings, and status enums.

ClubIntegrationUpdate.title: ClubIntegrationUpdate
ClubIntegrationUpdate.description:
Update request for a club's integration configuration.

The ``metadata`` dict is now bounded on three axes:
- max key count (``MAX_INTEGRATION_METADATA_KEYS``)
- max per-key length (``MAX_INTEGRATION_METADATA_KEY_LENGTH``)
- max per-value length (``MAX_INTEGRATION_METADATA_VALUE_LENGTH``)

Unknown envelope fields are rejected via ``extra="forbid"`` so future
refactors that accidentally echo request data back to the DB do not
introduce a mass-assignment surface.

EventFeedResponse.description: Public school feed response with catalog-freshness metadata.

EventPublicResponse.title: EventPublicResponse
EventPublicResponse.description:
Like EventResponse but without ``created_by``, so public detail
views do not leak creator UUIDs to unauthenticated callers.

EventResponse.title: EventResponse
EventResponse.description:
Full event payload returned from GET /events/{id} and used internally
for ownership checks.

``created_by`` is retained here because the field is load-bearing for
the authorization layer (``get_authorized_resource`` reads it); the
public list endpoint hides it via ``EventSummaryResponse`` which
omits the field entirely.

``occurrences`` is the canonical date list.

EventStatsResponse.title: EventStatsResponse
EventStatsResponse.description: Volatile public card stats loaded separately from the cached event feed.

EventSummaryResponse.title: EventSummaryResponse
EventSummaryResponse.description:
Payload for list/card views.

Description is included because the feed search matches event copy as well
as titles, hosts, locations, and food.

The owning club's display/link/social fields (``club_logo_url``,
``club_type``, ``club_page``, ``club_ig``,
``club_discord``) are
embedded read-time from the ``clubs`` row via the
``events.club_id`` FK so the event card can render without a second
fetch.

``created_by`` is intentionally omitted - this response is returned on
public GET /events/ and would otherwise leak the creator's Supabase
auth UID to anonymous callers.

GoingEventStatusResponse.title: GoingEventStatusResponse
GoingEventStatusResponse.description: Locks the going/not_going status contract at the OpenAPI boundary.

InteractionBatch.title: InteractionBatch
InteractionBatch.description:
Batch of interactions submitted from a single browser session.

**Trust boundary note on ``user_id``**: this field models the client's
*claim* of which user the batch belongs to.  The server verifies the
claim against the authenticated identity in ``interaction_service._validate_batch``
and 403s on mismatch.  The field is **advisory / diagnostic** -
never trust it for authorization or identity resolution in new code;
use the value resolved from the Bearer token instead.

Typed as ``UUID | None`` so the Pydantic boundary rejects arbitrary
opaque strings (e.g. ``"admin"``) at parse time - if the router-side
ownership check is ever removed during a refactor, impersonation
still cannot succeed because the payload won't even deserialise.

NotificationPreferenceUpdate.title: NotificationPreferenceUpdate
NotificationPreferenceUpdate.description: One preference-flip in a bulk update payload.

NotificationPreferencesBulkUpdate.title: NotificationPreferencesBulkUpdate
NotificationPreferencesBulkUpdate.description:
Settings-page payload: flip multiple toggles in one call.

The settings UI typically shows every type as a toggle; letting the
client send them in one request avoids N round-trips and lines up
cleanly with an UPSERT on the (user_id, notification_type) key.

NotificationPreferencesListResponse.title: NotificationPreferencesListResponse
NotificationPreferencesListResponse.description:
Every notification type's resolved enabled state for the user.

Includes types for which the user has no row (default-on); the
``enabled`` value is the resolved default in that case. Clients
render one toggle per entry.
